name: SECOND SHIFT — the agent team that never loses the thread
pitch: Second Shift is a live operations desk where four specialist agents share one attributed knowledge graph: every fact carries who asserted it, edges can contradict and supersede each other, and every action is a durable replayable record. Kill an agent mid-incident and the next one reads its open handover, replays the log from the exact checkpoint, honors the human approval already granted, and finishes the job — memory literally producing motion.
architecture:
ONE SPINE, FOUR ORGANS. The whole system is a single dispatch table lifted from unblock_mcp, fanned out into four surfaces, with LaserData as the only wire between services.

[1] SIGNAL (LaserData). A ~30-line Python producer tails the Wikimedia EventStreams SSE firehose (zero-auth, verified live, 50-100 ev/s) and publishes to topic `live.events` with `partition_key = wiki` so per-entity ordering is preserved. A pre-recorded 20-minute capture of the same firehose is replayable through the identical code path (file source == live source), so conference wifi can never kill the demo. LaserData is not just the ingress: it is the ONLY inter-service transport. Every memory write, every RocketRide tool call, every Guild handoff, and every human ruling is published as a record on `bus.*` topics. Consumers are LaserData consumer groups (server-assigned partitions, live rebalance on join/kill).

[2] MEMORY BUS (the reused unblock spine — this is the "least new glue" move). We lift the ~600-LOC skeleton out of unblock_mcp/server.py: the tool-schema builder, the `_VERB_DISPATCH` 4-tuple table (name -> METHOD, PATH, payload_builder, queueable), and the ~35-LOC `call_tool` router. We swap the 4th element from "Kaeva HTTP Edge Function" to "FalkorDB Cypher handler." Because the table already carries (METHOD, PATH), ONE table generates FOUR surfaces for free:
  - MCP streamable-http tools  -> consumed by RocketRide's `mcp_client` node
  - plain REST endpoints (FastAPI over the same table)
  - an auto-generated OpenAPI 3.0 spec -> fed straight into `guild integration operation create` (Guild's sandbox bans fetch/npm, so an OpenAPI Integration is the ONLY legal door — we build exactly one, not three)
  - a CLI for humans/rehearsal
This is unblock's own generated_tools.py OpenAPI->MCP codegen pattern run in reverse. Verbs: remember, relate, query, recall_path, handover_write, handover_read, ask, say, presence.

[3] MEMORY (FalkorDB). Node labels: :Event, :Entity(Editor|Page|Wiki), :Block(observation|decision|trace), :Agent, :Human. Edges: AUTHORED, MENTIONS, TAGGED, RELATES{relation in supports|contradicts|derived_from|supersedes|duplicates|references}, HANDED_OFF_TO{handover payload}. Two things unblock's flat SQL model could NOT do, which we get natively and demo: (a) edges are genuinely DIRECTED (unblock's contradiction_edges table has a `block_id_a < block_id_b` CHECK that forces undirected storage — a documented known limitation in relate-verb.ts:39-43; we drop it), and (b) variable-length traversal `[:RELATES*{relation:'supersedes'}]` for lineage resolution. HNSW vector index on Block.embedding gives hybrid retrieval: `db.idx.vector.queryNodes` for semantic entry, then Cypher hops for symbolic expansion. A port of unblock's sensing-gate (DEFAULT_SALIENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.15) runs as a vector-KNN lookup BEFORE every MERGE so the firehose can't bloat the graph. Runtime: falkordblite embedded (py3.12, no Docker — verified working on this box) bound to TCP 127.0.0.1:6399 so the Node/TS side and the FalkorDB Browser UI can attach to the same embedded DB; FalkorDB Cloud free tier is the shared cross-laptop mirror.

[4] MOTION (RocketRide). The decision loop lives in `motion/second-shift.pipe`, NOT in our Python. `agent_rocketride` (the Wave planner) is the orchestrator; attached via `control` edges are: `tool_falkordb` (first-party node — the agent itself issues Cypher with $params), `mcp_client` pointed at our Memory Bus, `tool_http_request`, `llm_anthropic` (Claude), `memory_internal`, and a researcher sub-agent-as-tool. Each wave the planner batches parallel calls — "LaserData tail + FalkorDB recall in the same wave, then decide." Our Python is ~40 lines: connect, use(pipe, ttl=0, pipelineTraceLevel="full"), set_events, send, stream the SSE `thinking` frames into the UI. Engine runs locally, MIT, dev key MYAPIKEY, already booted on this box.

[5] COORDINATION (Guild). Four published agents: `sensor-agent` (LaserData tail), `memory-agent` (FalkorDB recall/assert), `action-agent` (RocketRide execution), and an `orchestrator` that imports the other three as typed `/tool` sub-packages. The orchestrator runs `task.gather([sensor, memory])` — NOW and EVER fetched in parallel — then blocks on `ui_prompt` for human approval, then delegates to action-agent. Guild's runtime injects scoped credentials server-side so agent code never sees a raw key.

[6] IDENTITY (reused unblock, the sleeper feature). `http/session_persona.py` is copied near-verbatim: one Memory Bus process serves N distinct agent identities keyed on Mcp-Session-Id / per-request header, with zero cross-bleed. Every Cypher write is stamped `author_agent`. That is what makes the contradiction demo meaningful — the graph knows WHICH agent asserted what.

[7] SURFACE (app/). Single page: left = live force-graph canvas rendering Node/Edge objects streamed off the bus (nodes appear as events land); center = RocketRide trace panel narrating itself; right = decision card (ask/reply) + agent presence roster. The UI is a projection of the LaserData log, nothing more.

DATA FLOW: Wikimedia SSE -> LaserData `live.events` -> consumer group -> sensing gate -> FalkorDB MERGE -> anomaly published to `bus.incidents` -> Guild orchestrator wakes -> task.gather(sensor, memory-agent) -> memory-agent calls the Memory Bus REST surface (its Guild Integration) -> multi-hop Cypher -> contradiction detected -> ui_prompt to human -> ruling written back as a :Block{decision} with supersedes edges -> action-agent invokes the RocketRide .pipe -> the Wave planner calls tool_falkordb + mcp_client, acts, and writes a :Block{trace} with derived_from edges to the exact memories that caused it. Every one of those arrows is a durable LaserData record.

sponsor_integration.falkordb: LOAD-BEARING AS THE ONLY THING THAT CAN ANSWER THE QUESTION. Three proofs, each with a removal test. (1) SUPERSEDE-LINEAGE: `MATCH p=(old:Block{block_id:$id})<-[:RELATES*{relation:'supersedes'}]-(newest) WHERE NOT (newest)<-[:RELATES{relation:'supersedes'}]-() RETURN newest, length(p)` — 'you told me X, then Y; here is the CURRENT truth and the chain that got there.' A vector store and a SQL table structurally cannot do this in one shot. (2) CROSS-AGENT PROVENANCE: `MATCH (d:Block{block_type:'decision'})-[:RELATES*1..3]->(ev:Block)<-[:AUTHORED]-(a:Agent)` returns 'this action fired because of these 3 memories authored by these 2 agents.' (3) HYBRID GRAPHRAG: `CALL db.idx.vector.queryNodes('Block','embedding',10,vecf32($q)) YIELD node AS seed MATCH (seed)-[:MENTIONS]->(e:Entity)<-[:MENTIONS]-(neighbor)` — semantic entry, symbolic expansion, ONE query. We put `run_time_ms` (measured 4.8ms for 3 hops on this box) on screen next to the result. THE KILLER PROOF is the ablation: we run the identical incident twice, once with the graph seeded and once cold, and the SAME RocketRide agent picks a different, worse action. REMOVAL TEST: delete FalkorDB and there is no lineage, no contradiction detection, no attribution, and the agent's decision measurably degrades on camera. Runtime is falkordblite embedded (verified end-to-end on this Mac: 3-hop `[:KNOWS*1..3]`, path objects, HNSW index + `db.idx.vector.queryNodes`, cross-process persistence, TCP bind on 6399) so it cannot break from network loss during the pitch. Also: our directed-edge model is a genuine improvement over the prior art we ported from — we can show the constraint we dropped.
sponsor_integration.rocketride: LOAD-BEARING AS THE DECISION LOOP ITSELF, NOT A SUMMARIZER. The disqualifying anti-pattern for RocketRide is writing your own asyncio orchestration and calling their API once; we do the inverse. The agent loop, tool selection, parallel fan-out, retries, and sub-agent delegation live in `motion/second-shift.pipe` (~120 lines of JSON); our Python is ~40 lines of client (use/send/terminate + SSE stream). We use `agent_rocketride`, their Wave planner, which per wave plans a BATCH of tool calls and runs them in parallel — 'LaserData tail + FalkorDB recall in the same wave, then decide' is the reference data flow executing literally. Crucially we wire FalkorDB in through their FIRST-PARTY `tool_falkordb` node (query / list_graphs / get_schema, bundled in stable server-v3.3.1 — I confirmed the node registers in the live engine here), so judges watch the AGENT decide to call `falkordb.get_schema` and then `falkordb.query` with $params. And we mount the Memory Bus through their `mcp_client` node, so Guild and LaserData are reached THROUGH RocketRide rather than beside it: one graph, four logos, nothing bolted on. Visible proof: `pipelineTraceLevel='full'` + `set_events(token,['task','summary','flow','output','sse'])` streams `thinking` frames ('Calling tool_falkordb...') into the UI, and the VS Code canvas shows the node graph with live per-node tracing. REMOVAL TEST: delete the .pipe and there is no decision loop at all — nothing in our repo chooses a tool.
sponsor_integration.guild: LOAD-BEARING BY CONSTRUCTION, BECAUSE THE SANDBOX FORCES IT. Guild agent code may import only @guildai/agents-sdk, zod, and @guildai-services/* — no fetch, no npm, no Node built-ins. So every external system reaches our agents ONLY through a Guild Integration, and the delegation contract is enforced by the runtime, not by convention. We publish four agents: sensor-agent, memory-agent, action-agent, and an orchestrator that imports the first three as auto-generated typed `/tool` sub-packages (`import memoryAgentTool from '@guildai/<owner>~memory-agent/tool'`), inheriting their Zod input/output schemas. The orchestrator body is the reference flow: `task.gather([sensorTool(...), memoryTool(...)])` fetches NOW and EVER in parallel, then `ui_prompt` BLOCKS for a human ruling (options + recommendation + default-on-timeout — the shape lifted from unblock's ask/reply contract), then action-agent executes. THE JUDGE-FACING ARTIFACT is `guild session events <session-id>`: a real runtime trace showing orchestrator -> memory-agent -> ui_prompt -> action-agent with per-agent identities, token counts, and credential scopes. That is a verifiable coordination record, not a screenshot of an import. It also spans the kill: the trace shows agent A dying and agent B resuming the same session's work. REMOVAL TEST: delete Guild and the three sponsor integrations lose their tool surface entirely, the handoffs lose their type contracts, the human approval gate disappears, and every agent collapses back into one undifferentiated process.
sponsor_integration.laserdata: LOAD-BEARING AS THE ARCHITECTURE, NOT AN IMPORT — it is the ONLY interface between services, so it is unfalsifiable. Three proofs. (1) REPLAY AS TIME TRAVEL, our single strongest sponsor beat: because every event is durable and ordered, we `DROP` the FalkorDB graph on stage, replay the log from offset 0, and the graph REBUILDS to a byte-identical node/edge digest in seconds. 'Memory meets motion' has no more literal demonstration, and no other sponsor in the stack can do it. (2) CONSUMER GROUPS AS THE AGENT SUBSTRATE: our specialist workers join one named consumer group; the server assigns a partition per member and rebalances live. We kill a worker on stage and show its partitions redistribute with zero coordinator — that is also the mechanism behind the cold-resume wow. `partition_key=wiki` preserves per-entity ordering across the whole team. (3) EVERY ACTION IS A RECORD: memory writes, RocketRide tool calls, Guild handoffs, and human rulings all publish to `bus.*` topics via `laser.spawn_agent` (at-least-once, dedup, retry, DLQ, and an action GOVERNOR that can veto a publish). 'Every tool call this system ever made is on the log and I can replay any of them' is self-evidently deep. Our consumer ports unblock's four hard-won streaming invariants verbatim (enqueue-before-ack, stream-seq dedup, backpressure-not-drop, cancellation-safe teardown), so at-least-once redelivery is harmless — the FalkorDB write is a MERGE and the RocketRide call is fenced. CRITICAL SCOPE DISCIPLINE: LaserData's SDK also ships `laser.graph()` and `laser.memory()`, which would directly overlap FalkorDB's mandated role. We deliberately do NOT use them. Laser is strictly NOW + the spine; FalkorDB is strictly EVER. Saying that out loud to a judge is a credibility win, not a weakness. REMOVAL TEST: delete LaserData and there is no transport between any two services, no replay, no crash recovery, and no audit trail — the system does not start.

demo_script:
90 SECONDS. One laptop, three panels on one screen (graph canvas | RocketRide trace | decision card + agent roster), plus a phone on the podium for the human gate. Everything runs locally; nothing on stage requires network.

0:00-0:10 — OPEN COLD, NO SLIDES. Screen is already live: the graph canvas is visibly growing, nodes landing every few hundred ms off the Wikimedia firehose. "Agent teams forget everything when a session ends. Second Shift doesn't. This graph is filling from a live global event stream right now."

0:10-0:22 — MOTION IS REAL. Point at the LaserData counter: events/sec, offsets climbing, four consumer-group members with assigned partitions. Then the gate stat: "41,208 events ingested. 912 nodes. The salience gate rejected the rest as non-novel — this is memory, not a log dump." An anomaly surfaces on `bus.incidents`.

0:22-0:38 — MEMORY DOES SOMETHING NOTHING ELSE CAN. The RocketRide trace panel narrates itself in real time: "Calling falkordb.get_schema… falkordb.query…" — the AGENT chose those, not us. On the canvas a 3-hop path lights up as an animated trace, with `run_time_ms: 5` printed beside it. "That actor was flagged by a DIFFERENT agent, on a DIFFERENT wiki, six days ago — three hops, five milliseconds. A vector store cannot answer that."

0:38-0:55 — THE AGENTS DISAGREE, AND A HUMAN BREAKS THE TIE. Two Guild specialists assert conflicting reads; a red `contradicts` edge draws itself between two blocks, each labelled with the agent that authored it. The orchestrator REFUSES to act and fires `ui_prompt`. The phone lights up with a decision card: question, two options, the system's recommendation, a 60-second countdown and a default. A judge or teammate taps. The ruling lands in the graph as a `:Block{block_type:'decision'}` with `supersedes` edges to the loser. "Provenance, not vibes — we can query exactly which memories and which human ruling authorized this action."

0:55-1:15 — THE KILL (the money shot). Mid-remediation, `kill -9` the acting agent, live, on camera. Its LaserData partition rebalances to a new member. A fresh agent boots cold, reads its predecessor's OPEN handover node out of FalkorDB (summary / in_flight / next_steps / blockers / checkpoint), replays the log from that exact checkpoint offset, honors the human approval already granted, and COMPLETES the action. Flip to `guild session events <id>` — one continuous trace spanning both agents. "It didn't restart. It resumed."

1:15-1:26 — THE ABLATION (the load-bearing proof). Split screen: same incident, same agent, cold graph. Without memory it picks a different, visibly worse action. Then, in five seconds: `DROP` the graph, replay the LaserData log from offset 0, and the node/edge digest rebuilds identical. "Every event is durable. The memory is a projection of the log."

1:26-1:30 — CLOSE. "Every fact attributed to the agent that asserted it. Every action replayable from offset zero. Every handoff durable enough to survive the agent that made it. That's Second Shift." Leave the FalkorDB Browser open on the graph.

REHEARSAL RULE: the entire 90 seconds must run from ONE terminal script + one browser tab, with a pre-recorded screen capture as the hard fallback, and the incident replayed from a captured log — never live-sourced — so the only live thing on stage is the firehose in the background.

wow_factor:
THE KILL. Mid-demo, mid-remediation, with a human approval already granted, we `kill -9` the acting agent live on camera. Its LaserData partition rebalances to a new consumer-group member. A fresh agent boots completely cold — no session, no context, no prompt history — reads its predecessor's OPEN handover node out of FalkorDB (summary / in_flight / next_steps / blockers / checkpoint), replays the event log from that exact checkpoint offset, honors the human ruling it never personally received, and COMPLETES the action the dead agent started. Then we flip to `guild session events` and show ONE continuous trace spanning both agents. "It didn't restart. It resumed."

That single beat is the hackathon title executed literally — durable memory visibly producing motion — and it is only possible because all four sponsors are load-bearing at once: FalkorDB holds the handover and the provenance, LaserData supplies the durable checkpoint and the replay, RocketRide re-plans and re-acts from the recovered state, and Guild provides the agent identities and the trace that proves the handoff happened. Remove any one and the trick is impossible. It is also cheap for us — unblock already shipped the handover schema and its open->superseded lifecycle, so we are porting ~120 lines, not inventing a continuity protocol at 2am.

The two supporting beats compound it: agents that DISAGREE, with the contradiction drawn as a real directed edge and a human breaking the tie on a phone in under a minute; and the ablation — the same agent, the same incident, a cold graph, a visibly worse decision — which converts "we used FalkorDB" from a claim into a demonstration.

name: PALIMPSEST — the sentinel that remembers what the internet overwrites
pitch: Palimpsest watches the world's public knowledge being rewritten in real time and remembers every version — so when an edit that looks innocent in isolation is actually the fourth move in a coordinated campaign, our agent team catches it in three graph hops and two milliseconds, gets a human's approval, and fires a real action. Then we rewind: the identical live events replayed from offset zero into an empty memory, and you watch the same agents make the wrong call — that A/B is the proof the memory is load-bearing, not decorative.
architecture:
ONE laptop, five processes, one log spine. Everything between services travels as a LaserData record, so the log IS the architecture rather than an import.

[1] EDGE TAPS (Python, `realtime/`). `wiki_tap.py` holds an httpx stream on Wikimedia EventStreams SSE (https://stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange — zero-auth, verified live, ~50-100 ev/s) and publishes each edit to LaserData topic `wiki.edits` with `key=wiki` so per-wiki ordering is preserved across parallel consumers. 4 partitions, batch_length=200, linger_ms=50. This is the ONLY process that touches the public internet for ingest.

[2] LASERDATA PLANE (local `laser-stack` via Docker: iggy-server + laser-plane). Four topics: `wiki.edits` (raw signal), `mem.writes` (graph deltas for the UI), `agent.events` (orchestration trace), `actions` (what fired). Consumer groups give each agent lane a partition assignment with server-side rebalance on join/death. Delivery is at-least-once by design, so every downstream write is idempotent (MERGE) or fenced.

[3] MEMORY (FalkorDB, `memory/`). FalkorDBLite embedded, forced onto TCP via `serverconfig={'port':'6401','bind':'127.0.0.1'}` — VERIFIED on this box today: a completely separate process using the standard `falkordb` client connected and ran a variable-length `[*1..3]` traversal in 2.45ms. This is the key de-risk: the memory layer needs ZERO Docker, so if the conference wifi or Docker dies, memory still works. Two graph keys on one server: `sentinel` (warm, the real memory) and `sentinel_cold` (empty, the A/B target).
  Schema (labels/edges lifted from unblock's shipped taxonomy, not redesigned):
    (:Editor)-[:EDITED {ts,bytes,comment}]->(:Page)-[:ABOUT]->(:Entity)
    (:Claim)-[:CONTRADICTS|SUPPORTS|SUPERSEDES|DERIVED_FROM]->(:Claim)
    (:Agent)-[:AUTHORED]->(:Finding);  (:Agent)-[:HANDED_OFF_TO {…}]->(:Agent)
    (:Action)-[:DERIVED_FROM]->(evidence)
  Indexes: range on Editor.name / Page.title; HNSW vector on Claim.emb (dim 256, cosine) for semantic entry before symbolic expansion.
  A `graph_writer.py` consumer (group `graph-writers`) does salience-gate → Cypher MERGE → emit delta to `mem.writes`. NO LLM on this path: milliseconds, and nothing to hang on stage.

[4] MOTION (RocketRide, `motion/`). The engine is ALREADY BOOTED on this box (PID 9858, 127.0.0.1:5565, dev key MYAPIKEY). `sentinel.pipe` is the orchestration — not our Python. webhook → question → `agent_rocketride` (the "Wave" planner) wired with exactly one `llm_anthropic` (Claude Sonnet) + one `memory_internal`, and four tools attached by `control` edges: `tool_falkordb` (host 127.0.0.1, port 6401, allow_writes=true — a FIRST-PARTY FalkorDB node, so the agent itself chooses to call falkordb.get_schema then falkordb.query), `tool_http_request` (Discord webhook + GitHub API), `mcp_client` (our MCP server + Guild), and a `researcher` sub-agent. Driven with `ttl=0`, `pipelineTraceLevel="full"`, and `set_events(token,[task,summary,flow,output,sse])` so the SSE `thinking` messages stream into the UI as live narration.

[5] COORDINATION (Guild.ai, `agents/`). Four published agents: `watcher` (LaserData tail), `analyst` (FalkorDB multi-hop + claim extraction), `responder` (fires the action), and `orchestrator` which imports the other three as auto-generated typed `/tool` sub-packages — that import IS the handoff, with schemas inherited from the callee. `task.gather` fans out watcher ∥ analyst in parallel (now + ever), then `ui_prompt` blocks for human approval, then `responder` acts. Because Guild's sandbox forbids `fetch`, npm imports, and Node built-ins, ALL external I/O goes through ONE OpenAPI 3.0 Integration pointed at [6].

[6] BRIDGE (FastAPI, `app/bridge.py`). One service, one OpenAPI spec, one Guild integration (instead of three) — the single biggest schedule de-risk. Exposes /graph/query, /graph/write, /stream/tail, /stream/replay, /motion/dispatch.

[7] PROJECTOR UI (`app/index.html`). Single file, no build step, dark, huge type. Three panels: LIVE GRAPH (force-directed canvas, nodes/edges streamed from `mem.writes`, animated highlight tracing the multi-hop path when the analyst queries), AGENT LANE (Guild session handoffs + RocketRide SSE thinking), ACTION LOG (fired actions with clickable URLs). Plus a COLD|WARM split toggle for the replay A/B. The UI is purely a projection of the log — it holds no state of its own.

DATA FLOW: human edits a wiki page → SSE → LaserData `wiki.edits` → salience gate → FalkorDB MERGE (+ delta to UI) → Guild orchestrator gathers watcher ∥ analyst → analyst's 3-hop Cypher joins the live edit to the pre-baked historical corpus → RocketRide Wave agent decides escalate/ignore → ui_prompt → human approves → responder fires Discord + GitHub issue → the action is written BACK into the graph as (:Action)-[:DERIVED_FROM]->evidence.

sponsor_integration.falkordb: THE DECISION IS A FUNCTION OF A TRAVERSAL. The escalate/ignore verdict is computed from a 3-hop Cypher query joining the live edit → editor → prior campaign → a claim in the pre-baked historical corpus, i.e. across entities that arrived at different times from different sources. Falsifiable proof, run live on stage: replay the IDENTICAL event stream into an empty graph key (`sentinel_cold`) and the same agents, same model, same prompt return the OPPOSITE verdict ('benign, ignore'). Delete FalkorDB and the system provably cannot tell a lone edit from the fourth move of a campaign. It is not a KV store in a graph costume: we use variable-length `[:SUPERSEDES*]` lineage to resolve current-truth-from-revision-chains, and HNSW vector entry (`db.idx.vector.queryNodes`) followed by symbolic expansion through shared :Entity nodes — real GraphRAG, semantic entry + structural expansion, in one query. VERIFIED ON THIS BOX TODAY: Lite bound to TCP, cross-process standard-client connect, 3-hop traversal in 2.453ms. We put run_time_ms on screen. Second load-bearing role judges don't expect: the agents' OWN state lives here too — findings, provenance, and the handover rows that make the kill-and-resume beat work. NOTE we deliberately do NOT use laser.graph()/laser.memory(), which would cannibalize this role and muddy both sponsor stories.
sponsor_integration.rocketride: THE ORCHESTRATION IS THE .PIPE, NOT OUR PYTHON. The anti-pattern that would disqualify us is writing asyncio orchestration and calling RocketRide once to summarize — so the agent loop, tool selection, parallel fan-out, and retries all live inside the engine graph. `agent_rocketride` (Wave planner) plans a BATCH of tool calls per wave and executes them in parallel: fetching live context and recalling graph memory land in the SAME wave, then it decides — which is literally the hackathon's reference flow (NOW + EVER → decide + act) executing as engine primitives. Tool selection is the agent's: it calls falkordb.get_schema to learn the memory model, then composes parameterized Cypher itself. We use the FIRST-PARTY `tool_falkordb` node, so FalkorDB↔RocketRide is a vendor-built integration, not glue we invented — one wiring makes both sponsors load-bearing. Falsifiable proof: show the Wave trace with 2+ parallel tool calls in a single wave, then delete the tool_falkordb node from the .pipe and watch the agent lose the ability to decide. Our Python is ~40 lines; the orchestration is ~130 lines of .pipe JSON — their own 'build the runtime, not the stack' pitch, coming out of our mouth. Engine already booted here (PID 9858).
sponsor_integration.guild: THE TOPOLOGY AND THE HUMAN GATE ARE STRUCTURALLY UNREMOVABLE. Four published agents; the orchestrator can only call watcher/analyst/responder because Guild auto-generates their typed `/tool` sub-packages at publish time, and the caller inherits the callee's Zod input/output schemas — delete Guild and the handoffs lose their type contracts entirely. Guild's sandbox bans fetch/npm/Node-built-ins, which means every sponsor system (FalkorDB, LaserData, RocketRide) is reachable ONLY through a Guild Integration with server-side credential injection — agent code never sees a raw key. `task.gather` gives genuine parallel fan-out (now ∥ ever) over branded tool-call expressions. `ui_prompt` is the blocking human-in-the-loop gate before any real-world action fires. Falsifiable proof judges can READ rather than take on faith: `guild session events <session-id>` streams a server-side trace showing orchestrator → analyst → ui_prompt → responder with per-agent identities, tool calls, and token counts. That is a verifiable coordination artifact, not a screenshot of an import statement. It also answers 'why not just a Python script' — agents as independent security principals with scoped credentials.
sponsor_integration.laserdata: IT IS THE ONLY THING CONNECTING THE FIVE SERVICES, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THE WINNING BEAT POSSIBLE. Every inter-service message — raw signal, graph deltas, orchestration trace, fired actions — is a LaserData record on one of four topics; the UI holds no state and is purely a projection of the log. Kill the plane and all five processes stop exchanging: a two-command falsification. But the headline role is that OUR STRONGEST PROOF IS A LASERDATA PRIMITIVE: the cold-vs-warm A/B is implemented as a durable replay from offset 0 (a fresh consumer at polling='first') re-deriving the entire graph from scratch into an empty key. 'Watch me rewind the last hour and re-derive the memory' is the literal embodiment of memory meets motion, and no other sponsor in the stack can do it. Consumer groups are the substrate for the agent lanes — one partition per member with server-side rebalance, so we can kill an agent on stage and show work redistribute with no coordinator. Partition key = wiki preserves per-entity ordering across the whole team. HONEST FRAMING we say out loud before a judge asks: LaserData does not supply data, it is the nervous system carrying a live feed we point at it — the feed is Wikimedia's public firehose.

demo_script:
90 SECONDS. Three roles fixed in advance: H2 DRIVES (sole hand on keyboard), H3 NARRATES (never touches a key), H1 holds a PHONE. One projector, one browser window, three panels already live and the firehose pre-warmed for 45+ minutes so the graph is dense and the actor has real history.

[0:00-0:10] HOOK — screen is already alive. Nodes are landing on the LIVE GRAPH panel every fraction of a second, ambient, unprompted.
H3: "This is Wikipedia being rewritten, right now. Fifty edits a second, worldwide. Every node you see arriving is a real human, editing a real page, in the last few seconds." (No slide. No title card. The motion is the opening.)

[0:10-0:25] IT IS REAL, AND YOU CAN CHECK — H1 holds up the phone, visibly types, hits save on a Wikipedia sandbox page.
Within ~2 seconds a new node blooms on the projector, ringed and labeled with the editor name.
H3: "That just went from his phone, through Wikimedia's public firehose, through LaserData, into our graph. Sub-second. Pull out your own phone after this and verify the feed — it's zero-auth and public."
(This beat is a human action we perform, never a rare natural event. Never build a beat on chance.)

[0:25-0:45] THE MONEY SHOT — THREE HOPS. The analyst agent wakes on that node. An animated path traces across the graph, lighting up four nodes in sequence, ending deep in a differently-colored cluster.
H3: "That editor isn't new to us. Three hops: this edit → this account → a campaign we flagged forty minutes ago → a claim in a corpus we ingested this morning. Different sources, different times, one query."
On screen, large: `run_time_ms: 2.45` and the Cypher itself.
H3: "Three hops. Two milliseconds. A vector store cannot answer that question — there's no such thing as 'semantically similar to a four-step causal chain.'"

[0:45-1:00] THE PROOF — THE REWIND. This is the beat that wins. H2 hits one key. The screen splits COLD | WARM.
H3: "Same events. Same model. Same prompt. On the right, our memory. On the left, I'm replaying the identical LaserData log from offset zero into an empty graph."
The cold panel's graph builds in fast-forward; both agents return a verdict, side by side:
  COLD → "Routine edit. No action."   WARM → "Coordinated campaign, 4th move. Escalate."
H3: "That's the whole thesis. Delete the memory and the same agents make the wrong call. The memory isn't decoration — it's the difference between those two answers."

[1:00-1:15] COORDINATION + A HUMAN + A REAL ACTION. AGENT LANE panel scrolls the live Guild trace: orchestrator → gather(watcher ∥ analyst) → analyst returns → ui_prompt.

name: Ringleader
pitch: Ringleader watches a live global event firehose and catches coordinated manipulation campaigns that are invisible in any single event — because it remembers every actor, page, and co-edit that ever happened as a directed property graph, and answers in one 3-hop Cypher query what a vector store structurally cannot. Kill it mid-investigation and it restarts cold, reads its own handover node out of the graph, resumes from its committed stream offset, and finishes the case.
architecture:
COMPONENT MAP (everything on the critical path runs on localhost; only Guild's control plane needs the network).

[1] FEED PRODUCER (realtime/producer.py, ~25 LOC) — subscribes to the Wikimedia EventStreams SSE firehose (https://stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange, zero auth, verified live, ~50-100 ev/s). Publishes every edit to LaserData topic `signal.raw`, partition key = wiki, so per-wiki ordering is preserved across parallel consumers. Hot-swappable backup producer for USGS earthquakes (same topic contract, different source) if Wikimedia throttles.

[2] LASERDATA LOG = THE ONLY BUS. Not a side-channel — it is the sole interface between every service. Topics: `signal.raw` (firehose), `signal.salient` (post-sensing-gate), `case.opened`, `case.decision`, `action.executed`, `agent.handoff`. Consumer group `graph-writers` with N members (server assigns one partition per member, rebalances on join/leave). auto_commit=disabled, commit-after-handle. Managed primitives (Views/Changes/State/Graph) are NEVER used — Log only — so the same code runs on local laser-stack, LaserData Cloud, or bare Apache Iggy. Every capability beyond Log is gated behind `await laser.capabilities()`.

[3] SENSING GATE (realtime/gate.py) — between the consumer and the graph. Embeds the candidate edit summary, runs a FalkorDB vector-index KNN, and drops writes whose top-1 cosine distance is below the novelty threshold. Ported from unblock's sensing-gate (threshold 0.15). Without it a firehose floods the graph with near-dupes and the ring query drowns.

[4] FALKORDB = MEMORY OF RECORD (memory/). falkordblite embedded, bound to TCP 127.0.0.1:6399 so Python, Node, and the falkordb-browser all attach to one graph. Nodes: :Actor, :Page, :Wiki, :Event, :Case, :Agent, :Assertion, :Action. Edges: [:EDITED {ts,bytes,summary}], [:ON], derived [:CO_EDITED_WITH {window_s,count}], [:IMPLICATES], [:AUTHORED], [:RELATES {relation}] over the 6-value unblock vocabulary (supports|contradicts|derived_from|supersedes|duplicates|references) stored DIRECTED, and [:HANDED_OFF_TO {handover_id,status,summary,in_flight,next_steps,checkpoint}]. Indexes: range on Actor.name/Page.title/Case.id, HNSW vector on Event.emb for hybrid GraphRAG entry.

[5] THE BRIDGE (app/bridge/, FastAPI) = KEYSTONE, one artifact with four consumers. Endpoints: POST /cypher, POST /recall, GET /ring, GET /graph (nodes+edges projection), POST /stream/publish, GET /stream/tail, POST /act, POST /handover. Built on unblock's 4-tuple dispatch table so every verb flows through ONE request chokepoint. It simultaneously serves: (a) the REST API for the UI, (b) an MCP surface mounted into RocketRide via its `mcp_client` node, (c) the single OpenAPI 3.0 spec behind ONE Guild integration (instead of three), (d) the seed script. This one decision is what makes Guild affordable in 8 hours.

[6] ROCKETRIDE = EXECUTION ENGINE (motion/ringleader.pipe). Self-hosted MIT engine already booted on 127.0.0.1:5565 with built-in dev key. Graph: webhook_1 -> question_1 -> agent_rocketride "Commander" (Wave planner, max_waves=12) with control-attached llm_anthropic (Claude Sonnet), memory_internal, tool_falkordb (FIRST-PARTY node: falkordb.query/list_graphs/get_schema, allow_writes=true, graph=ringleader), tool_http_request (feed lookups), mcp_client (our bridge), and a researcher sub-agent with its own llm_anthropic (Haiku) + memory_internal -> response_answers. Each wave the planner batches FalkorDB recall (EVER) and live fetch (NOW) IN PARALLEL, then decides. pipelineTraceLevel="full", ttl=0, set_events([task,summary,flow,output,sse]) streams `thinking` messages to the UI.

[7] GUILD.AI = AGENT ORG + GOVERNANCE (agents/). Four published agents: `sensor-agent` (owns the LaserData ops on the bridge integration), `memory-agent` (owns the FalkorDB recall ops), `motion-agent` (owns /act -> RocketRide), and `commander` which imports the three as typed /tool sub-packages. commander runs task.gather([sensor, memory]) for parallel NOW+EVER, then ui_prompt blocks for a human approval on any consequential action, then hands off to motion-agent. Every handoff, credential scope, and agent identity is in the `guild session events` trace.

[8] UI (app/web/) — single page: live force-graph canvas fed from /graph, an SSE ticker of RocketRide `thinking` events, a case panel, and an offset/lag readout for the LaserData consumer group. It is a pure projection of the log + the graph; it holds no state.

DATA FLOW (the mandated one, executing literally): SSE -> LaserData `signal.raw` -> consumer group -> sensing gate -> FalkorDB MERGE -> ring Cypher -> if ring_score > threshold, publish `case.opened` and POST the Guild trigger -> Guild commander gathers sensor+memory in parallel -> ui_prompt human gate -> motion-agent -> RocketRide wave (falkordb.get_schema, falkordb.query, tool_http_request in one batch) -> decision -> `action.executed` on the log -> written back to FalkorDB as (:Action)-[:RELATES {relation:'derived_from'}]->(:Event) so every action has clickable provenance -> UI renders.

sponsor_integration.falkordb: ROLE: memory of record, and the layer that answers the question nothing else in the stack can. THREE WAYS IT IS NON-REMOVABLE. (1) The ring query is a single variable-length Cypher over a time window returning Path objects — MATCH p=(a:Actor)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(b:Actor)-[:EDITED]->(:Page)<-[:EDITED]-(c:Actor) with ts-window and DISTINCT actor constraints — and we put run_time_ms (~5ms measured) on screen next to the result. No single stream event and no vector store produces that answer. (2) THE ABLATION IS THE PROOF: identical live event, replayed twice — once against a cold graph, once against the seeded graph — and the RocketRide agent selects a DIFFERENT, demonstrably worse action (dismiss vs quarantine). We record both terminal outputs side by side as a gate artifact. That A/B is the strongest possible answer to 'is the graph decorative?'. (3) The agent's own continuity lives in the graph: the handover node ((:Agent)-[:HANDED_OFF_TO {status:'open', summary, in_flight, next_steps, checkpoint}]->(:Agent)) is what makes cold-restart resume work, so deleting FalkorDB also breaks the demo's headline moment. HYBRID GraphRAG is real, not claimed: HNSW vector index on edit-summary embeddings gives semantic entry (db.idx.vector.queryNodes — sorted ASC, because the score is a DISTANCE not a similarity), then symbolic multi-hop expansion through shared :Page and :Actor nodes. We also fix a real defect we inherited: unblock's SQL edge table forces undirected storage via a block_id_a < block_id_b CHECK, so 'supersedes' and 'derived_from' lose direction; FalkorDB stores true direction, which we demo as supersede-lineage resolution ('you told me X, then Y — here is the current truth and the chain'). FALLBACK LADDER (this is the LOWEST-risk sponsor and therefore the local-of-record): falkordblite embedded — verified end-to-end on this exact Mac, no Docker, no daemon, no network, `from redislite.falkordb_client import FalkorDB` (NOT `import falkordblite`), Python >=3.12 — started with serverconfig={'port':'6399','bind':'127.0.0.1'} so the standard falkordb client, the npm client, and falkordb-browser all attach to the same embedded DB. Tier 2: Docker server if any teammate's laptop has Docker (buys the Browser UI on :3000 free). Tier 3: Cloud free tier if the three of us need one shared graph. The graph file path/port lives in ONE shared config constant — Lite persistence is per-file-path and two people pointing at different paths silently fork with no error.
sponsor_integration.rocketride: ROLE: the execution layer — the .pipe file IS the orchestration, not a summarizer we call once. THE DISQUALIFYING ANTI-PATTERN would be writing our own asyncio loop and calling RocketRide to phrase the answer; we do the opposite: the agent loop, tool selection, retries, parallel fan-out, and sub-agent delegation all live in the RocketRide graph. demo_script:
90-SECOND STORYBOARD. Screen is one page: force-graph canvas (left, 60%), RocketRide thinking-ticker + case panel (right, 40%), LaserData offset/lag strip along the bottom. A phone on the table is the human-approval surface. Everything runs on localhost; wifi is not on the critical path.

[0:00-0:10] HOOK — canvas is sparse, the bottom strip shows offsets climbing.
Say: "A single edit is never suspicious. A campaign is. Ringleader catches coordinated manipulation that is invisible in any one event."

[0:10-0:25] MOTION (LaserData). Nodes bloom onto the canvas in real time as the Wikimedia firehose lands; the offset counter and per-partition lag tick visibly.
Say: "This is a live global firehose going through LaserData. Every event is durable, ordered, and partitioned — and it is the only interface between every service in this system. Nothing here talks to anything except through the log."

[0:25-0:40] MEMORY (FalkorDB) — THE RING LIGHTS UP. A subgraph highlights; an animated path traces actor -> page -> actor -> page -> actor. Cypher and result drop into the panel with run_time_ms visible.
Say: "Three accounts, four pages, twelve minutes. No individual edit crosses any threshold. One three-hop Cypher query over everything that ever happened — five milliseconds. A vector store cannot produce that answer; it has no edges to walk."

[0:40-0:55] DECIDE (RocketRide). The ticker narrates itself: "Calling falkordb.get_schema" / "Calling falkordb.query" / "Calling tool_http_request" — the last two in the SAME wave, side by side.
Say: "The orchestration is not my Python. It's a RocketRide pipeline. The agent chose to read the graph's schema, then query it, and it pulled live signal in the same parallel wave. Now it's what's happening and what ever happened, together, deciding."

[0:55-1:05] HUMAN GATE (Guild). A ui_prompt blocks: "Quarantine 3 accounts, watch, or dismiss?" A teammate taps QUARANTINE on the phone; the agent resumes. Cut to a terminal running `guild session events <id>`.
Say: "Four Guild agents — sensor, memory, motion, and a commander that called the first two in parallel and then stopped for a human. This is the real trace: every handoff, every identity, every credential scope. Session id's in the README."

[1:05-1:20] THE KILL — the money shot. Presenter runs `pkill -f commander` mid-case. Screen goes dead. Restart cold.
Say: "Watch." (restart) "It just read its own open handover node out of FalkorDB, re-attached to its LaserData consumer group at its last committed offset — and it's finishing the case it was in the middle of. It remembered, and it kept moving."
Canvas resumes mid-trace; case panel fills in the remaining steps and closes the case.

[1:20-1:30] THE ABLATION — the load-bearing proof, and the close. Split terminal: same event replayed twice, cold graph vs seeded graph. Left: "DISMISS — insufficient signal." Right: "QUARANTINE — ring of 3, confidence 0.87."
Say: "Same event. Left has no memory and throws it away. Right remembers and catches the ring. That's the whole thesis." End card: four gate artifacts, four sponsor logos, one line each on what breaks if you remove it.

BACKUP: a full screen capture of a clean run is recorded at T+6:45 and kept one keystroke away. If any live element misbehaves we cut to tape and keep narrating — we never debug on stage.

GUILD'S SANDBOX FORBIDS fetch(), Node built-ins, and all external npm packages — every external call must become an OpenAPI-generated Integration through a six-step publish cycle. Three integrations (FalkorDB, LaserData, RocketRide) would consume most of the sprint. MITIGATION: ONE bridge, ONE OpenAPI spec, ONE integration, and the spec is written and published FIRST (hour 2) before the bridge is finished, so the long pole runs in parallel with implementation.

GUILD'S PUBLISH -> /tool -> npm install -> REBUILD CYCLE SERIALIZES AGENT DEVELOPMENT. The orchestrator literally cannot import a specialist until that specialist is published, and every specialist schema change forces the whole loop again. MITIGATION: specialists published first with schemas FROZEN at hour 3, orchestrator last; hour-7 fallback is an llmAgent with useWorkspaceAgents:true, which discovers workspace agents dynamically with no publish cycle and still produces the visible handoff trace.

DOCKER IS NOT INSTALLED ON THE BUILD MAC and laser-stack requires Docker Engine 25+ / Compose v2.20+. Every LaserData README leads with a docker command that will simply fail. MITIGATION: Docker Desktop pre-installed on at least two laptops as a pre-event task; FalkorDB deliberately does NOT depend on Docker (falkordblite is verified working without it), so a Docker failure costs only the LaserData tier and not the memory layer. Second tier is LaserData Cloud free tier — but it is rate-limited (docs say 100 KB/s, console says 200 KB/s) so a firehose WILL throttle; we throttle the producer to match rather than discovering it on stage. LASERDATA IS v0.0.1, PUBLISHED THE DAY BEFORE THE EVENT — near-zero community answers, and its managed primitives (Views/Changes/State/Graph) raise UnsupportedError without the laser-plane sidecar. MITIGATION: the architecture uses ONLY the Log primitive, which works on every tier including bare Apache Iggy; everything else is gated behind `await laser.capabilities()`. We also copy the shipped examples verbatim rather than improvising, and keep laser-example-photon-market open as a known-working reference. Known trap pre-registered: the examples hardcode iggy:iggy@ but laser-stack prints iggy:laser@, which fails as what looks like a network error.

PYTHON VERSION FRAGILITY ACROSS ALL THREE PYTHON SPONSORS. The system python here is 3.9.6; falkordblite needs >=3.12, laser-sdk >=3.10, and rocketride >=3.10 — and on 3.9 `pip install rocketride` SILENTLY installs 1.0.0, a materially different API, instead of failing. Same class: falkordblite's import path is `from redislite.falkordb_client import FalkorDB`, not its package name. MITIGATION: one pinned 3.12 venv baked into every run script, no bare pip installs, and a 60-second preflight script that asserts versions and import paths before anyone debugs anything else.

FALKORDB FOOTGUNS THAT LOOK LIKE SUCCESS. (a) The vector index score is a DISTANCE, not a similarity — sorting DESC shows judges the WORST matches while appearing to work (verified: identical vector scored 0.0, neighbour 0.0061). (b) FalkorDB is an openCypher SUBSET — Neo4j Cypher and APOC do not paste. (c) falkordblite persistence is per-FILE-PATH, so two teammates on different paths get silently different graphs with no error. MITIGATION: an assert-on-ordering unit test for the vector path, every non-trivial query validated against the running instance in hour 1, and the graph path/port in one shared config constant.

THE COMPOSITE ROCKETRIDE .pipe HAS NEVER RUN AS A UNIT. Provider-name traps (the registered service is `mcp_client`, not `tool_mcp_client`), two easily-conflated wiring keys (`input` = data flow, `control` = tool/LLM/memory attachment declared on the TOOL pointing back at the agent), a hard requirement of exactly one llm and one memory_internal per agent, and ttl != 0 killing long agent fan-outs mid-demo with 'Your pipeline is not currently running'. MITIGATION: build up node-by-node from the two-node pipeline already verified on this box, client.validate() before every use(), and keep the minimal pipe as a hot fallback.

LLM LATENCY, RATE LIMITS, OR A COLD MODEL DURING THE PITCH. GraphRAG-style ingest is an LLM call per chunk and finalize() is O(total graph size), not O(change size) — calling it in a streaming loop gets quadratically slower on stage. MITIGATION: the graph is pre-baked before the demo; the LIVE path is raw parameterized Cypher MERGE with zero LLM calls; agent max_waves is capped; and a recorded backup capture exists from T+6:45.

AT-LEAST-ONCE DELIVERY MEANS A CRASH REDELIVERS — and the kill-and-resume demo deliberately crashes things. A non-idempotent action would fire twice live on stage. MITIGATION: every graph write is a MERGE, every action record is keyed by case_id + decision hash, and commits happen only after side effects land.

CONFERENCE WIFI AT FRONTIER TOWER. MITIGATION: the entire critical path is localhost — falkordblite, laser-stack, and the RocketRide engine all run on the machine. Only Guild's control plane needs the network, and that is the one segment with a recorded fallback. We drill a wifi-off run at hour 7.

SCOPE SPRAWL — four new sponsor SDKs is an infinite surface and the team's own worst enemy. MITIGATION: the hour-5 gate list is the definition of done; feature freeze at T+6:30 is absolute; anything not required by a gate is cut without discussion. Explicitly out of scope and named as such: GraphRAG-SDK's text-to-Cypher path (experimental, off by default, and it swallows all exceptions so a broken query looks identical to 'no data'), QueryWeaver (it is Text2SQL, not text-to-Cypher, and would add a Postgres dependency for a fourth logo we already have), and LaserData's own graph()/memory() primitives (they overlap FalkorDB's mandated role and would muddy both sponsor stories).

A JUDGE READS A FIELD NAME AND FINDS IT DECORATIVE. unblock's source_proven/responder_proven attestation flags are FALSE in production with a live-attested forgery path — if we port a trust badge we must either make it actually load-bearing or label it honestly. Same principle applies to any 'confidence' or 'verified' field we render. MITIGATION: nothing on screen claims a property we cannot demonstrate on request.

TWO MOMENTS, BACK TO BACK, THAT NO SINGLE-SPONSOR PROJECT CAN COPY.

FIRST — THE KILL. Mid-investigation, on stage, the presenter kills the commander process. The screen goes dead. It restarts cold, with no in-memory state whatsoever: it reads its own open handover node out of FalkorDB (summary, in_flight, next_steps, checkpoint), re-attaches to its LaserData consumer group at its last committed offset, and finishes the case it was in the middle of. That is the hackathon's title executed literally — durable memory visibly producing motion — and it is structurally impossible without BOTH mandated layers doing real work: FalkorDB restores what it knew, LaserData restores where it was. Remove either and the resume breaks in a different, demonstrable way.

SECOND — THE ABLATION. The same live event replayed twice from the log, once against a cold graph and once against the seeded graph, side by side. Cold: "DISMISS — insufficient signal." Warm: "QUARANTINE — ring of 3, confidence 0.87." Identical input, identical code, different memory, materially different action. This is the strongest possible answer to the only question that actually matters to these judges — "is the graph load-bearing or decorative?" — and it is an experiment, not a claim. It also demonstrates a LaserData capability nothing else in the stack has: only a durable ordered log lets you feed the exact same reality to two different agents.

Supporting beat if there is time: a rewind to offset 0 that re-derives the entire graph from scratch in seconds, with node and edge counts asserted equal to the live-built graph — the system's entire memory is reproducible from its motion.
